The commonest Stan regression idiom — `y ~ normal(beta1 + beta2 * x, sigma)` with x a data vector — never reaches `normal_id_glm` at any optimization level today. The existing rewrite needs a matrix predictor and runs only above default level, so everyday models compile to the plain vectorized path at about 54 instructions per element. This pass emits the glm call for both shapes: the matrix form at default level, and the scalar-intercept plus slope-times-vector chain as a plain call, since an Eigen column vector binds the design argument directly and the intercept binds the weight. Multi-column forms wrap with `append_col`; the wrap measures 37 instructions per element and does not eat the win.

The glm interior computes an analytically simplified gradient, so this changes numerics at default level: on the two real models gated, log density agrees to 2 ulp and gradients to 1.7e-15 relative, but draws differ. Sampler comparisons over three reps and four chains agree at distribution level, and one long-horizon control favors the emitted form.

Measured on a real regression model: the likelihood subtree drops from 54.3 to 9.5 instructions per element (−82%), the whole run −56%; a second model with the wrapped form loses 66% of its likelihood complex.

Pattern discipline: ten negative controls stay silent at both levels, and a full-tree census of 1,233 models finds exactly two changes per level — both intended. Self-contained with stock stan math. The natural upstream form is the same pass gated behind `--Oexperimental` until the numerics change is agreed.
